results.correct_value: North Fork Quinault River Trail about 12 miles to the river ford at Sixteen Mile Camp, cross the river, then off-trail directly up Lawson's north side (not via Low Divide / Skyline Trail).
results.evidence: Beta, waypoints, itinerary, timing, descent_text, bail and bivy all use the river-ford line below Lawson's north side; only approach and watch_out[4] send the party to Low Divide and the Skyline Trail. The NPS trail page puts the Sixteen Mile river ford ~12 mi up and Low Divide ~3.5 mi beyond it; Wikipedia says the summit rises 3,800 ft above the North Fork in 1.3 mi, and the Mazamas North Ridge listing starts the climb from the North Fork trail and goes up a gully from the creek.

results.correct_value: The ford/leave-trail point is the North Fork crossing at Sixteen Mile Camp, about 12.2 mi from the trailhead; round trip to the summit about 25 mi. The ford elevation is not settled.
results.evidence: NPS camp spacing (Wolf Bar ~2.5, Halfway House +2.6, Elip ~4 from Wolf Bar, Sixteen Mile ~5.7 from Elip) puts the Sixteen Mile ford at ~12.2 mi; trail databases give the ford at 12.1 mi / 'about 12 miles in'. The Mazamas North Ridge listing gives 25 mi round trip, matching 12 mi in plus the summit day. The waypoint 7.2 mi, itinerary 10 mi, and the later pins (8.7, 9.5 mi) are therefore wrong; the gully and summit pins have no sourced distance so they are set to null. The ford waypoint's 1,050 ft elevation looks too low (the summit is 3,800 ft above the river, implying ~1,600 ft; the camp entry says 2,021 ft) but no two sources state it, so elev is left unchanged (unresolved).

Wikipedia gives the easiest route as class 2 hiking; the Mazamas North Ridge listing gives only a club rating (A/B), no class. No second independent source states a class for this route, and the row itself is split (grade, overview, descent_text, partner_requirements say Class 3; beta and bivy say Class 2; itinerary a Class 3-4 step). Left unchanged.

The Mazamas listing rates the climb for spring, summer and fall (winter harder) without a window; NPS notes the Sixteen Mile ford is hazardous in snowmelt and heavy rain, which argues against June but states no window for the climb. No two sources give a season for this route, so season, best_season and seasonal_guidance are left as is.

results.evidence: NPS lists fords at Wild Rose Creek, Elip Creek and 16-Mile, and describes the Sixteen Mile crossing as the North Fork itself, knee to thigh deep. An independent trip report and hiker reviews describe the trail crossing the river by a ford at Sixteen Mile Camp. '16-Mile creek' in hazards/watch_out is the river crossing, not a creek.

results.correct_value: The North Fork Quinault is not a wilderness quota area; permits are still reserved online.
results.evidence: The NPS wilderness reservations page lists the quota areas (Sol Duc/Seven Lakes, Grand Valley, Royal Lake, Ozette coast, Lake Constance, Flapjack, Upper Lena, Hoh sections, and since 2024 the East Fork Quinault) and says non-quota permits are not limited; the North Fork Quinault is not among them. Washington's National Park Fund names the same quota areas. So the pro tip's claim that Wolf Bar and Elip Creek fill fast is unsupported.
